def factor_drawdown_depth_atr_gated(df):
    df_copy = df.copy()
    peak = df_copy["close"].rolling(63, min_periods=63).max()
    dd = (df_copy["close"] - peak) / peak
    depth = (-dd)
    high_low = df_copy["high"] - df_copy["low"]
    high_close = (df_copy["high"] - df_copy["close"].shift(1)).abs()
    low_close = (df_copy["low"] - df_copy["close"].shift(1)).abs()
    tr = pd.concat([high_low, high_close, low_close], axis=1).max(axis=1)
    atr = tr.rolling(63, min_periods=63).mean()
    normalized_depth = depth / atr.replace(0, np.nan)
    high_resvol = df_copy["style_gate_resvol_high"] > 0
    factor_values = np.where(high_resvol, normalized_depth * 0.5, normalized_depth)
    factor_values = pd.Series(factor_values, index=df_copy.index)
    factor_values.name = "factor_drawdown_depth_atr_gated"
    return factor_values

Lightweight modifier: regime gating from drawdown_stress_ratio_gated that dampens the signal by 50% during high residual volatility to reduce noise. The cross-sectional rank transform enhances comparability across assets as relative drawdown severity is economically meaningful.
style_gate_rationale: High residual volatility indicates idiosyncratic noise; dampening the drawdown depth signal in such regimes reduces erratic rank reversals and improves stability.
